themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key, and the thing being measured often shifts while you measure it. So the models start small: a fixed panel of questions, a consented panel of people, or a standing holdout they run forever, just to have something honest to grade against.
themes.evidence: Today's answers on cross-channel incrementality all start with randomized holdouts or regional shutoffs and warn that platform bidding re-optimizes against the test, echoing answer engine optimization (model drift swamps the intervention), identity resolution (no truth set for who is the same person), and B2B buying-group signal loss (few accounts ever buy).

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot look inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. The best anyone offers is watching from outside: planting fake records, expiring every list you send, or judging spend only by outcomes you can see yourself.
themes.evidence: On downstream consent and deletion the models propose canary profiles, single egress gates, and lists that expire in two weeks while agreeing that trained models cannot unlearn a person; the same opacity drives the incrementality answers (platforms control both the treatment and the evidence) and the ad supply integrity answers.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls are about meaning and worth, not data: whether a headline implies a promise, whether evidence really backs a claim, what the word customer means, what one more message is worth. No formula settles these, because the disagreement has budget attached.
themes.evidence: All three models say generative content governance fails on implied claims and context, the semantic context layer answers call conflicting definitions of active customer a political fight rather than a modeling gap, and journey orchestration answers say no objective function can be politically neutral.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported list cannot be called back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Safe agent execution answers converge on a proxy or gateway with spend, rate, and audience caps because sends and spend cannot be rolled back; downstream consent answers route every export through one gate, and journey orchestration answers build a shared send log with veto power.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Many of these problems stall because the party holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. So the models either try to make honesty pay better than hiding, or they stop waiting for cooperation and work only with what they already own.
themes.evidence: Agentic traffic answers offer fast lanes, discounts, and signed delegation tokens because agents profit by looking human; journey orchestration answers note channel owners are paid on local numbers, and incrementality answers say platforms have no reason to expose auditable treatment assignment.
